description_full: Criteo S.A., a technology company, provides platform to connects the commerce ecosystem for brands, agencies, retailers, and media owners to drive measurable business outcomes in North and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. It operates in two segments, Retail Media and Performance Media. The Retail Media segment connects brands to shoppers at the digital point of sale through personalized ads that appear on retailer websites and across the open internet. The Performance Media segment encompasses commerce activation, monetization, and services that enable advertisers to reach and convert consumers across channels. It also offers Commerce Max, a suite of retail media demand-side tools that allow brands, agencies, and retailers to plan and buy media across retailer and open internet inventory with closed-loop, product-level measurement, and return-on-ad-spend optimization; Commerce Growth, a solution for continuous customer acquisition and retention for performance marketers and agencies; and GO, an AI-driven solution that automates campaign creation and optimization. In addition, the company provides Commerce Yield, which offers monetization solutions that help retailers and marketplaces maximize the value of their digital assets through inventory and data management, packaging, and in-depth insights; Commerce Grid, a commerce-focused supply side platform for media owner data and inventory monetization; and Criteo Shopper Graph, which derives clients' proprietary commerce data, such as transaction activity on their digital properties. It serves retail, travel and marketplaces, and other commerce companies. Criteo S.A. was incorporated in 2005 and is headquartered in Paris, France.

financial_summary: Criteo S.A. is a small-cap communication services business with a $887M market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 36%.

The business throws off $208M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.15× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 82× is fortress-like.
Management returns a meaningful 17.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares.

sector_headwinds.text: Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Volatile returns on capital suggest the moat is narrower than a snapshot ROIC implies
Altman Z in the grey zone — financial health warrants monitoring
Insiders are overwhelmingly selling (100% sell ratio) — the people who know the business want less of it
Advertising-cycle exposure and content/regulatory risk — a single platform policy shift or ad-spend contraction cascades through the P&L quickly.
Cord-cutting acceleration and audience fragmentation — legacy distribution bundles unravel faster than subscription revenue can replace them.
AI-generated content commoditisation — as creation costs collapse toward zero, content libraries lose pricing power and differentiation narrows.

sector_tailwinds: Reinvestment rate supports 12% organic growth capacity — capital is compounding inside the business
Trading at a 51% margin of safety to estimated fair value — a real cushion against errors in the estimate
Market is pricing in lower growth than the company has historically delivered
Valued at a 68% discount to sector median EV/EBITDA
Piotroski score 8/9 — financials improving across profitability, leverage and efficiency
Financial quality scores above most Communication Services peers

Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 23.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 27.4% (vs the 8% bar).

Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.15x.
ROE of 13% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $219.4M.

growth: Revenue has compounded at -1.2% over 3 years and -1.3% over 5 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 80% of profits supports about 12.3% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Capex runs 3.1x depreciation (5.3% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 6, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.

own: Insiders own a modest 2.7%, and institutions hold 83%.

It returns 17.1% a year to shareholders (17.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 5.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 3,504 employees, each generates about $555K of revenue, in line with the Communication Services median.
That works out to $60K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.4M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
